speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the cause of your fatigue, malaise, and weight loss, can you describe any other symptoms you are experiencing, such as fever, night sweats, or changes in your appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: 71-year-old male. The patient complains of fatigue and malaise over the last few months. He also reports an unintentional weight loss of 18.1 kg over the past 6 months. He does not recall any changes in diet or exercise routines that could explain the weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant amount of weight loss. Have you experienced any night sweats, fevers, or noticed any lumps or swollen glands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue and malaise. I also have Significant unintentional weight loss, No change in diet or exercise.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned significant weight loss and fatigue, but I need to know if you have any abdominal pain, changes in bowel habits, or difficulty swallowing? Also, have you noticed any blood in your stool or changes in urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Has a history of diabetes mellitus type II, hypertension, non-seminomatous testicular cancer treated in the past, and hypercholesterolemia. Social history: Currently smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and drinks a glass of wine daily. Denies any illicit drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your medical history. Do you have any specific pain in your chest, back, or abdomen, or have you noticed any visible lumps or swelling anywhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, night sweats, or significant changes in bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of smoking and testicular cancer, I need to check for malignancy or metabolic issues. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Urinalysis, and CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC Elevated with lymphocytosis, Hemoglobin Normal to slightly decreased, Platelets Normal to decreased. FLOW CYTOMETRY: Presence of monoclonal B lymphocytes with a phenotype consistent with CLL/SLL. COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL: NORMAL READINGS. URINALYSIS: NORMAL READINGS. CT CHEST/ABDOMEN/PELVIS: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The flow cytometry results showing monoclonal B lymphocytes are diagnostic for Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). I will review the full extent of the disease staging with you.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
